# YM15: 山高水长 Shangao Shuichang, "Hills High and Waters Long"

Malone calls it The Drill Field.

Wave 1 · Yuanming Yuan · 3D: `/reconstruction/3d.html?b=YM15` · Page: `/scenes/#YM15` · Row: `research/buildings/YM15-shangao-shuichang/`

## What it was

山高水长 Shangao Shuichang, "Hills High and Waters Long", the open ground in the south-west corner of Yuanming Yuan, south-west of 万方安和. A tower facing west, nine bays, with linked hills behind it, a stream before it and level ground of several qing in the middle (S05 j81:15b; E1519). The editors date the tower to 1726 and give its first name as 引见楼; behind it a rear court with side halls and a landing by a cross pavilion; before it a slanted riding track, an earth target wall to the north-west, and the thirteen courts 十三所 to the south-east that served the firework nights (S361 v2 p.147; E1529). Used from Yongzheng to Xianfeng for the New Year feast of Mongol princes and envoys in great tents, guards' archery, and fireworks at the Lantern Festival (S05; E1519, E1521, E1528, E1535); in 1795 the Dutch embassy was received in a tent here (S02 pp.167-170; E1526). Daoguang reviewed the 精捷营 here in 1839 (E1328, E1346) and Xianfeng shot with guns here in 1855 (E1518). Burned with the garden in October 1860; nothing visible today (E1011).

From the inventory row: **built** 1726; **destroyed** 1860 (S05, S02, S08, S01, S361).

## The scene itself

### The leaf of 1744, its poem and preface

Leaf 15 of the 1744 album. Qianlong's preface: "在園之西南隅地勢平衍構重樓數楹" (in the south-west corner of the garden, on level ground, a storeyed tower of several bays). He says the far hills and near fields lie open to view, that foreign princes are feasted here at New Year with fish-and-dragon shows and wrestling, and that in ordinary times the guards practise archery. The poem praises the feast as uniting inner and outer peoples ("内外一家連") (S40, printed in S05 j81:18a; E1515).

### How later sources differ

日下旧闻考 (1780s) adds a horizontal stele at the left bay carrying the edict of 1752, with the edict of 1778 on sparing the bravest soldiers cut on its back (S05 j81:15b-18a; E1519). The 养吉斋丛录 calls the place 西厂, the West Yard, and lists the banquet of the 19th of the first month with wrestlers and acrobats (S202; E1521); 檐曝杂记 describes 3,000 lantern dancers before the tower forming the characters 太平万岁, then fireworks (S213; E1520). Jiaqing set a rain altar here in 1812 (S47 p.118; E1527). Xianfeng's note of 1855 mentions Qianlong's earth wall with a carved poem, used for gun practice (S360 p.145 item 152; E1518). On the 21st day of the 7th month of 咸丰六年 (1856) the Xianfeng emperor came by boat and landed "至山高水长后阁扇下船，出前门", at the rear of the tower, then left by its front gate: the tower had a water landing behind (east) and its gate on the field side (S210; E1524). The Yangshi Lei sheets for this place are mostly 道光-同治 (S13 pp.157-172; E1532), one Qianlong sheet shows seven Mongol tents and the fireworks before the tower (S310 样018-1号; E1535).

Drawings: 样018-4-1, the 山高水长 tower plan of 道光十一年 1831 (presentation sheet with yellow slips and paste-overs, E1534); 样018-1 of the Qianlong reign, the layout of seven Mongol tents and fireworks for the New Year banquets in front of the tower, the largest tent c. 24 m across (E1535); record 7326 is a second plan of the scene without catalogue data (E1533). The field was c. 460 x 280 m per the mhymy record (S310 rec. 7326).

## Interior and setting

### Interior

Plaque 山高水长 in Qianlong's hand; the stele at the left bay with the edicts of 1752 and 1778 (S05 j81:15b; E1519). During feasts the emperor sat in a great tent 武帐 set on the field, not in the tower (S337; E1528, E1535). Van Braam (1795) describes the imperial rooms elsewhere as small, neatly furnished, with a few books and curiosities (S02 pp.167-170; E1526); that passage is not about this tower.

### The garden around it

Level grass field, the largest open space in the garden (S02 p.83; E1525), backed on the east by a chain of low hills ("後擁連岡") with a stream in front ("前帶河流") (S05 j81:15b; E1519). Across the stream Malone records a straight horse run of half a mile from a round tower in the north to 藻园 in the south, with a small shrine to General Liu Meng by the round tower (S02 p.83; E1525). An earth target wall to the north-west (E1529, E1518). On feast days Mongol tents and firework frames stood on the field (E1535, E1520).

P0015 shows the open field closed by low wooded hills, with the long two-storey 山高水长楼 seen end-on from the south: a 卷棚歇山 roof, a grey brick gable wall below, wood-coloured lattice along the upper storey and no red columns; a chain of small grey courts runs south-east of it. No tents or targets are drawn. (S08 P0015, crop ym15_c1)
